items.title: Delhi’s toxic air: Athletes must keep training, but many can’t afford to leave
items.summary: With winter in full swing and pollution levels rising, most Delhiites stay indoors. Athletes, however, don't have that option. Even with the GRAP (Graded Response Action Plan) Stage-III in effect and the CAQM (Commission for Air Quality Management) advising postponements of sports competitions, training continues. In this report, Khushi Jaiswal speaks to athletes and coaches in the capital. High-repetition training, they say, demands heavy oxygen intake, and in the polluted air, they bring breathing difficulties, dry throats and persistent coughing. One parent even says that her daughter has been on anti-allergy medication for a week. Some athletes leave Delhi to train in places like Bengaluru, Odisha or hill stations in nearby states, and a few have even gone abroad. But leaving Delhi comes with a cost which many families can't afford. As a result, many are forced to train even when the AQI (air quality index) exceeds 400. Athletes in Delhi University, meanwhile, say that the DU Sports Council tournaments are still going ahead, with no postponements. Watch our report. items.summary: A doctor’s arrest on October 16 drew fresh attention to the police action against opponents of Vedanta’s proposed bauxite mine in Odisha’s Sijimali hills. Dr Randall Sequeira is not the only one behind bars. Newslaundry looked at a few other arrests: Laxman Naik, a martial arts instructor arrested alongside Dr Sequeira; Hiramal, a farmer jailed since August; and Lingaraj Azad, an activist held since March. All three are named in multiple FIRs alongside hundreds of unidentified persons, and all have had bail pleas rejected. The FIRs offer a window into the pressure on a movement that began in 2023 across at least 40 villages. Since then, at least 40 cases have been registered. Newslaundry has seen copies of five, which name at least 155 accused and refer to a further 900 unidentified persons. The allegations in them are yet to be tested in court. The mining project will require extensive forest land to be cleared in the Tijimali hill range of the Eastern Ghats and the direct displacement of at least two villages. Many residents depend on farming or herding for their livelihoods. They cultivate rice and vegetables on small plots. The project would force them to move elsewhere. Concerns have been raised before about human rights violations amid action against protesters. Police have not yet responded to Newslaundry ’s questions. items.title: IIM Ahmedabad, Tata group train over 100 in-house lawyers in business strategy, leadership
items.summary: The Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (IIMA) and Tata group have trained over 100 in-house lawyers from Tata Group companies through a specialised programme aimed at equipping corporate legal professionals with skills in business strategy, leadership and organisational decision-making. The initiative, conceived in 2022 by IIMA Professor of Strategy MP Ram Mohan and Tata Sons Group General Counsel Sidharth Sharma , seeks to address the changing expectations from in-house lawyers, whose responsibilities increasingly extend beyond legal advice to strategic business decisions. MP Ram Mohan and Sidharth Sharma Explaining the rationale behind the programme, Professor Ram Mohan said that the competencies required of corporate lawyers differed significantly from those expected in private practice. "The capabilities required to navigate the demands from in-house lawyers including persuasion, conflict management; long-term strategic thinking; understanding how critical management decisions are made; and the ability to build and motivate teams etc differ in nature and degree from those ordinarily required of a lawyer in private practice," he said. Sharma said that economic liberalisation had substantially transformed the legal profession, particularly the role of in-house counsel. "This is particularly visible in the growing role of in-house lawyers, who are expected to take ownership of issues that are both legal and strategic or business-related," he said. Batch 4_2026 He added that corporate lawyers must understand business imperatives, collaborate across organisations and provide stakeholders with actionable guidance. Launched in 2023, the programme was designed as a three-to-five-day on-campus certificate course at IIMA. Its curriculum includes leadership, strategic thinking, finance, marketing, team building, persuasion, conflict management, crisis management, legal risk management and Gandhian philosophy. The programme has entered its fourth edition, with participation from over 100 senior and mid-level lawyers across Tata group companies. Madhav Uppuluri , General Counsel of Tata Consultancy Services, said executive thinking, leadership and influence had become essential qualities for in-house lawyers. " The Leadership and Management Development Programme, a unique collaboration between IIM Ahmedabad and Tata Sons Legal, is designed to build exactly these capabilities and transform in-house counsel to next generation legal leaders, " he said. A Bench of Justices Arijit Banerjee and Apurba Sinha Ray observed that the decision to backtrack from the sale agreement appeared to be a case of "regime revenge" by the Mizo government that took charge in December 2023. "It does appear to us that this is a case of ‘regime revenge’. The Government cannot renege on a promise made and acted upon by a citizen to his detriment, only because there is a change in regime," the Court said. items.title: Karnataka High Court grants bail to POCSO accused after victim's family agrees to their marriage
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently granted bail to a man accused of penetrative sexual assault under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act after the victim's family agreed to their possible marriage. Justice Venkatesh Naik T noted that the accused and the victim's family had reached an understanding that the possibility of marriage would be considered once the victim attains the legally prescribed age. The Court also recorded that police had completed investigation in the case and filed a chargesheet against the accused. "Having regard to the completion of the investigation, the affidavits filed by the parties, the no-objection expressed by the victim’s mother and the understanding arrived at between the families, I am of the opinion that the continued detention of the petitioner may not be necessary, provided adequate conditions are imposed to safeguard the interests of the victim and ensure the petitioner’s presence during trial," the Court said. Justice Venkatesh Naik T The accused was booked in the case alleging offences of penetrative sexual assault, aggravated penetrative sexual assault, rape, causing hurt, and criminal intimidation on the basis of a complaint filed on May 22. He was arrested a day later and remained in judicial custody since then. After a trial court rejected his bail on September 26, the accused approached the High Court. Taking into account the complainant's no objection to the bail and the completion of the investigation, the Court on November 5 ordered the release of the accused. With regard to the settlement arrived at between the families, the Court said, "Though the said understanding cannot, by itself, determine the merits of the prosecution or nullify the statutory provisions, the same can be taken into consideration as one of the relevant circumstances while considering the prayer for bail." Advocate Sadik Kanvi appeared for the accused. High Court Government Pleader Dayanand Sangreshi appeared for the State. Advocate Ameena HS represented the complainant.

items.title: Calcutta High Court allows Chhath Puja worship by devotees on private property
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Friday allowed devotees to offer prayers for Chhath Puja on private property, subject to strict supervision by the police and volunteers. [Kanchan Dubey and Ors v. The State of West Bengal and Ors] A Bench of Chief Justice Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge and Justice Om Narayan Rai was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by a group of women seeking permission to celebrate Chhath Puja for a few thousand devotees on a private property belonging to the Shib Krishna Debutter estate, located on the Ganga river bank at Rashbari ghat in Bally, Howrah. The counsel for the petitioners submitted that the rituals would be completed within 19 hours. "How can we pass a writ of mandamus allowing people to barge into private property?" the Court asked. Additional Advocate General Billwadal Bhattacharyya, appearing for the State, assured the Court that the government would take appropriate steps to monitor the crowd. items.summary: The Madras High Court has expressed surprise over a claim that even Brahmins can get Other Backward Classes (OBC) reservation benefits by converting to Christianity and joining the Church of South India (CSI) under Tamil Nadu's existing reservation framework. items.title: Stamp duty on arbitral awards must exclude interest component: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently held that stamp duty on an arbitral award must be calculated on the principal amount awarded and not on the interest component even where such interest forms part of the total sum awarded by an arbitral tribunal. [ Patel KNR Infrastructure Ltd v. NHAI ] Justice Jasmeet Singh held that Section 23 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 makes it clear that the mere inclusion of an interest component in an instrument cannot result in an enhanced stamp duty liability. "The interest component cannot be included in the computation of stamp duty merely because it forms part of the total amount awarded by the Arbitral Tribunal," the Court observed. Justice Jasmeet Singh The Court delivered the ruling while dismissing a review petition filed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) against an April 2024 order directing it to pay the balance interest due to Patel KNR Infrastructure Limited under an arbitral award. NHAI argued that the arbitral award of ₹18.34 crore was insufficiently stamped because stamp duty had been calculated only on the principal amount of ₹11.75 crore, excluding approximately ₹6.49 crore awarded as interest. It contended that the deficiency rendered the award unenforceable. Patel KNR, however, relied on Section 23 of the Stamp Act to argue that interest could not be included in the stamp-duty calculation. The Court accepted this submission. "In this regard, Section 23 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 is relevant. The provision specifically stipulates that where interest is expressly made payable by the terms of an instrument, such instrument shall not be chargeable with duty higher than that with which it would have been chargeable had no mention of interest been made therein." It further reiterated that review proceedings cannot be used to reopen issues already considered. "A review cannot be treated as an appeal in disguise or an opportunity to re-agitate issues which have already been considered," the Court said. Finding no error apparent in its April 2024 order, the Court dismissed NHAI's review petition. Central Government Standing Counsel Balendu Shekhar, along with advocates Tanisha Samanta, Krishna Chaitanya, Divyansh Singh Dev and Rajkumar Maurya represented NHAI. items.title: Chandigarh to host India International Disputes Week 2027 in January
items.summary: The second edition of India International Disputes Week (IIDW) will be held in Chandigarh from January 9 to 13 in 2027. Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , along with other Supreme Court judges, and several High Court judges are expected to attend the event. During the five-day program, arbitrators, counsel, in­-house teams and policymakers from India and abroad will deliberate under the theme of "Rising Solutions to Emerging Conflicts" on what comes next for emerging conflicts and dispute resolution. IIDW 2027 will feature keynote addresses and panel discussions across a wide range of subjects, including: • Alternative Dispute Resolution and Arbitration •⁠ ⁠Artificial Intelligence and Data Protection •⁠ ⁠Financial Crimes •⁠ ⁠Private Equity and Tax •⁠ ⁠Intellectual Property •⁠ ⁠ESG and Energy •⁠ ⁠Construction •⁠ ⁠Family Law •⁠ ⁠Defense Further details and registration information can be accessed at: www.disputesweek.com IIDW is a regional–global platform focusing on arbitration, litigation, mediation and policy dialogue. The first edition of the IIDW was held between March 7-11 in 2026 under the aegis of the Punjab and Haryana High Court. It brought together over 2,000 participants, more than 60 international delegates and nearly 150 speakers. items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently quashed a criminal case against a snake rescuer accused of capturing and photographing a King Cobra. Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde on November 2 quashed the proceedings initiated against snake rescuer Dr. P Gowri Shankar. The Court held that the allegations did not establish that the petitioner had kept the snake in captivity, killed or injured it or uploaded its photographs on social media. “It is not the allegation that the petitioner has kept the king cobra in captivity, killed or injured [it], or uploaded the photograph,” the Court observed. Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde The case against Shankar was that he had captured a King Cobra and had taken its photograph while in captivity and also allowed others to take its photographs. The complaint against the petitioner was filed based on the social media publication where the petitioner was found in a video uploaded by a third person. The petitioner sought to quash trial court proceedings after he was booked for various offences under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. The petitioner contended that the charge sheet materials did not establish that he had hunted or captured the King Cobra. He also argued that the photographs relied upon by the State showed the snake in an open forest area and not in captivity. The State argued that the charge sheet materials indicated that the petitioner had permitted others to photograph the King Cobra and had caused the photographs and videos to be uploaded on social media. The High Court noted that the State had failed to substantiate that the King Cobra had actually been captured by the petitioner. “What is seen from the photographs produced along with the charge sheet is that the king cobra was found in the forest in an open space and it was not kept in captivity,” the Court said. The Court noted that the photographs were published on social media and not recovered from the petitioner. It also observed that he had repeatedly reported rescued King Cobras to forest officials. “That being the position, the Court cannot take a view that the petitioner has committed any of the offences as alleged in the complaint,” it held. Hence, the Court proceeded to quash the case. Advocate Akshay Swamy appeared for the petitioner. Additional State Public Prosecutor MV Anoop Kumar appeared for the State. items.title: Finance firms cannot use goons to seize vehicles over loan default: Allahabad High Court
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently held that finance companies seeking to repossess vehicles over loan defaults must do so only through a legal forum, either judicial or arbitral [Sadab Ahmad v State of UP and others] A Division Bench of Justices JJ Munir and Indrajeet Shukla observed that if a finance company is permitted to exercise its right to seize the vehicle by force, it would be virtually arming a private party with the coercive authority of the State. "No doubt, it is true, as often said, that in a contract, parties legislate for themselves, but that principle cannot imaginably be carried to the extent, where the terms of the contract are actually imbued with legislative force empowering parties to enforce terms, deciding for themselves and executing it too, as if they were judicial or quasi-judicial fora, deciding a lis and then executing the decision," the Court said. Justice JJ Munir and Justice Indrajeet Shukla In the judgment passed on October 26, the Bench added that while the Supreme Court has protected the finance companies from criminal prosecutions for taking away vehicles in such cases, they are not allowed to use force merely because a clause in the agreement authorizes them to seize the vehicle from the borrower. "The right of the finance company engrafted into a hire-purchase agreement to seize the chattel, the vehicle here, purchased on hire-purchase, gives an enforceable right no doubt to the finance company, but that enforcement has to be done through a process known to law. It cannot be done by force employing goons, styled as agents," the Court emphasised. The vehicle could not be taken into possession by employment of recovery agents, who would waylay the hirer or his driver and seize it at gunpoint, the Bench further said. The Court was dealing with the petition moved by one Sadab Ahmad who said a goods carrier vehicle purchased by him in 2023 with finance of the HDB Financial Services Limited was seized by the company's recovery agents on August 9. Ahmad was driving the vehicle when he was intercepted by the men acting on behalf of HDB Financial Services, the Court was told. He submitted that he had regularly paid his dues and had already cleared 31 out of the total 45 instalments. Ahmad was later told by the financial company that the vehicle was not seized in connection with his own loan account, but on the ground that he had stood guarantor in regard to the vehicle loan of another person. items.title: Karnataka HC dismisses MLA Yatnal's plea to quash defamation case filed by Congress MLA Patil
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Thursday refused to quash a criminal defamation case filed against expelled BJP MLA Basanagouda Ramangouda Patil Yatnal over remarks he made against Congress MLA Shivananda S Patil during a media interview broadcast on the YouTube channel of Gadinada Kranti on April 30, 2025. Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde dismissed a plea filed by Yatnal challenging the criminal proceedings. In doing so, the Court rejected Yatnal's argument that the trial court had erred in taking cognisance of Patil's complaint without first examining a witness who could speak to whether Patil’s reputation had been lowered in that witness's estimation. The High Court held that, at the stage of taking cognisance, a magistrate need not invariably insist on examining a witness other than the complainant to establish that the complainant's reputation has been lowered in the witness's estimation. Whether such a witness needs to be examined would depend on the nature of the alleged imputation and the facts of the case. “The expression ‘in the estimation of others’ in Explanation-4 to Section 499 of IPC or 356(1) of BNS (dealing with the crime of defamation) cannot be construed as having mandated, that in every case at the stage of taking cognizance and issuing the process, that a witness other than the complainant must be examined and said witness must state that in his own estimation the complainant’s reputation is lowered,” the Court held. Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde The defamation case against Yatnal stems from remarks he allegedly made about Patil on April 30, 2025. The remarks came amid a political confrontation in which Yatnal reportedly challenged Patil and Congress MLA Vijayanand Kashappanavar to resign from the Assembly and face him in by-elections. The two leaders were among those who had criticised Yatnal over his remarks concerning Prophet Mohammed. Yatnal, in his response, allegedly questioned Patil's parentage and claimed that his family had adopted the Patel surname for political reasons. He also accused Patil of cheating the Panchamasali community and taking money during a padayatra. The remarks also contained personal attacks on Patil's character and political conduct. Patil filed a criminal defamation complaint against Yatnal on July 18, 2025. On January 24, 2026, a magistrate took cognisance of the complaint and summoned Yatnal. items.title: Leaving all disputes to arbitration could stall growth of law: Former Supreme Court Justice Ravindra Bhat
items.summary: Leaving all disputes to arbitration could eventually slow the development of law, Former Supreme Court Justice S Ravindra Bhat cautioned even as he acknowledged that Indian courts have increasingly limited their interference with arbitral awards. Speaking at the Dubai Arbitration Week 2026, Justice Bhat said legal principles have evolved through robust judicial enquiry and the limited scope for reviewing arbitral awards raises a broader question about how new legal concepts would develop. “So if you leave everything to arbitration, as we all believe that all disputes should be arbitrable, I think there will be a time when the growth of law will be static,” he said. Justice Bhat was speaking at “Four Courts, One Award: Judicial Perspectives, Cross-Border Advocacy & the Great Common Law Debate” , organised by the Indian Institute of Arbitration and Mediation in association with Balfaqeeh Advocates & Legal Consultants and Providence Law Asia. The panel also featured former Abu Dhabi Courts judge Ahmed Bakry , Providence Law Asia Managing Director Abraham Vergis S C and JSA Partner Sidharth Sethi . DSK Legal Partner Dinesh Pardasani moderated the discussion. Justice Bhat clarified that he was not advocating a radical change. However, advances in technology and emerging questions concerning damages and other legal doctrines required reflection on how courts should respond. He said judicial scrutiny helped develop legal principles. He questioned how new doctrines, including those concerning damages and technology, would evolve if disputes were increasingly resolved through arbitration with limited court review. He explained that an award could survive judicial scrutiny so long as it met the internationally accepted public policy threshold. This prompted the question of how the law would grow when disputes were increasingly resolved through arbitration. On judicial intervention in India, Justice Bhat said the position has changed over the past decade, with the Supreme Court repeatedly emphasising that interference must be minimal, and public policy could not accommodate every objection to an award. “But the courts are more constrained now in the sense that unless something is egregious and it appears on the face of the award, the enquiry doesn't proceed further,” he said. items.title: ‘Closing meat shops during PM’s visit is fascism’: Former Karnataka HC judge Nagamohan Das
items.summary: Former Karnataka High Court judge HN Nagamohan Das on Friday, November 13, criticised the closure of meat shops in parts of Bengaluru’s Anekal taluk ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit. He called the directive an instance of fascism and an infringement of citizens’ fundamental rights. “The right to food is a fundamental right. You eat what you want, let them eat what they want, and let me eat what I want. Who are you to come and dictate what we eat?” Nagamohan Das said. His remarks came after the Bengaluru Urban district administration ordered the closure of meat shops within the limits of Jigani Town Municipal Council and Kallubalu Gram Panchayat in Anekal taluk from 6 am on November 12 to 4 pm on November 13. The order was issued ahead of Modi’s visit to the area for the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram. Speaking at a symposium on ‘Decentralisation and Planned Development’ organised by the Karnataka State Policy and Planning Commission at Gandhi Bhavan, Nagamohan Das questioned the rationale behind linking the Prime Minister’s visit to restrictions on food choices. “I don't know whether you like it or not; the Prime Minister visiting is a matter of pride for us and for our state. Let him come! But why should meat shops be closed? If liquor shops were closed, I might be somewhat satisfied with it. How do you link the closing of mutton shops to the visit of the Prime Minister? If this isn't fascism, then what else is it?” he asked. The symposium was organised to mark the birth centenary of former Karnataka Chief Minister Ramakrishna Hegde. The November 10 order, issued by Bengaluru Urban Deputy Commissioner and District Magistrate P.S. Kantharaju, invoked Section 163(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, citing security concerns. The police sought the restriction, stating that anti-social elements might disrupt law and order during the Prime Minister’s visit. The retired judge also warned against the return of fascist tendencies in different forms, recalling the sacrifices made to defeat fascism in the country's democratic history. “It was as a result of all these sacrifices that we pushed back fascism. items.title: TN cops allege suicide after lorry driver found dead in station restroom
items.summary: A 42-year-old lorry driver, who had gone to Chekkanoorani police station in Madurai in connection with a complaint, was found dead in the station's restroom on Saturday, November 14. The police have claimed that he died by suicide. According to reports, the deceased have been identified as Balakrishnan, a resident of Alagarnayakanpatti in Theni district, who worked as a lorry driver for a company involved in transporting goods. On November 3, Balakrishnan was transporting around 60 bags of cardamom from Thevaram in Theni to Madurai when the lorry he was driving allegedly caught fire near Valandur canal in Madurai's Usilampatti area and the fire destroyed the cardamom bags. Following the incident, the company manager, who had sent the cardamom, raised suspicion over missing bags and submitted a complaint to the police. Based on the complaint, the police asked Balakrishnan to appear for an inquiry at Chekkanoorani police station and also to assist the police in examining CCTV footage related to the incident. Balakrishnan had also approached the police station with a complaint over the fire that destroyed the bags. According to the police, he was questioned on Friday, November 13 and they found contradictions in Balakrishnan's complaint and asked him to remain at the station overnight. He was housed in the inspector's room before he went to the restroom and was found unconscious the next morning. He was rushed to Government Rajaji Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. A postmortem examination is yet to be conducted. The police claimed that Balakrishnan may have died by suicide after alleged discrepancies in his complaint came to light. Following the incident, Chekkanoorani police station Inspector Muthu and woman constable Kalaiselvi, along with other personnel who were on duty at the time, were suspended. The police have preserved the CCTV footage from the station as part of the investigation. Balakrishnan's relatives staged a protest outside the police station and raised questions about how a person brought to the station for questioning was found dead in its restroom. South Zone Inspector General of Police (IGP) Vijendra Bidari said the case had been transferred to the Crime Branch-Criminal Investigation Department (CB-CID) for further investigation. He also said that a judicial inquiry would be conducted and that the CCTV footage from the police station are being examined.
